external_inputs.used: Buchdahl Theorem 11, journal p.297 / PDF p.12, also stated journal p.288 / PDF p.3. Applies only to actual compact complex surfaces, not to complex fourfold Y.
Section 9, Remark 3, journal p.77 / PDF p.78: tangent Hom(I,O); Theorems 1 and 2, journal pp.83-84 / PDF pp.84-85: universal space and finite dimension. PDF p.81 displays local Banach gluing model.

proof_checks: Global N leaves are generated by actual unstable complex surfaces and the already global stable central complex curves. Their transverse angle does not degenerate at Z.
Preservation of slow labels makes N invariant under each monodromy; preservation of sigma then preserves the characteristic line contained in Eu.

Identification of the new characteristic line uses Birkhoff sublinearity and two legitimate Fubini stages: actual unstable absolute continuity, then a regular holomorphic foliation inside that unstable complex surface.
Both central errors vanish only after the second central line has been identified globally.
All compact complex Lagrangian fibres are actual submanifolds before any surface theorem is used.
A surface homeomorphic to T4 is Kahler by Buchdahl; the exterior H1 cohomology ring makes its Albanese map degree one; pullback surjectivity on H2 plus a Kahler form rules out contracted curves.
The classifying map into Douady is proved continuous by single normal graphs and continuous split ideal projections. No analytic structure on B is presumed at this stage.
An injection from a real 2m-manifold into a local analytic embedding of dimension m forces an open image; its defining ideal vanishes, including possible nonreduced structure.
Trivial normal bundle is not used alone as an unobstructedness theorem; the maximal actual topological family is essential.
The universal evaluation map is locally biholomorphic by normal section evaluation. Disjointness of actual fibres gives the holomorphic submersion.
The recovered complex two-dimensional base is again a torus by the surface lemma and supplies nonzero monodromy-invariant closed holomorphic forms.
